question: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-cooperation Movement in February 1922 after which incident?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chauri Chaura Incident**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chauri Chaura incident:-**

 
 
• On February 5, 1922, a mob of protesters participating in the Non-cooperation Movement at Chauri Chaura in Uttar Pradesh, India, clashed with the police.
 
• The protesters set fire to the police station, killing 22 policemen.
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-cooperation Movement in February 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident. (Hence option 1 is correct)**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh massacre:-**

 
 
• It was also known as the Amritsar massacre, took place on April 13, 1919, in Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar, Punjab, British India. 
 
 
 
• **Kakori train robbery:-**
 
 
• **It was an armed robbery that took place on August 9, 1925, on a train in central Uttar Pradesh, India. **
 
• It was organized by the Indian revolutionaries of Hindustan Republican Association (HRA).
 
 
 
• **Bomb Blast in central assembly:-**
 
 
• On April 8, 1929, a bomb exploded in the Central Legislative Assembly in Delhi, India.
 
• **The bomb was thrown by Bhagat Singh, a member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). **
 
• The bomb blast was intended to protest against the British rule in India.
